extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and applicants) on identifying, documenting, and limiting functional claim elements under 35 U.S.C. §112(f) during prosecution, with particular attention to software claims written in functional terms. Advises when to require structure, when to treat claims as means-plus-function, and how to record equivalence and invocation on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a claim element is a functional claim element
rubrics_metrics.description: First, examiners should determine whether any given claim element is a functional claim element. Often the answer will be obvious because the element is structural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the element does not contain obvious structure, whether or not it uses the words “means for,” examiners should ask the applicant to clarify on the record whether the claim element is intended to invoke section 112(f). This determination is the starting point for further action (clarification, amendment, or rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document invocation of §112(f) in written record and interview summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: When the issue arises during prosecution, examiners should ensure the record reflects whether claim elements invoke §112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While that will normally happen during the written record of rejection and amendment, if the issue arises during an interview the examiner should specify in the interview summary whether or not the claim elements discussed invoke section 112(f). Explicit documentation avoids ambiguity about claim scope later in litigation or prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require applicant to point out corresponding structure when invoking §112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does intend to invoke section 112(f), the applicant should be required to point out the corresponding structure in the specification that supports that means-plus-function claim element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no such structure in the specification, the claim should be rejected as indefinite. In some circumstances it may be appropriate to clarify on the record what the applicant regards as equivalent to that structure (e.g., when distinguishing prior art). Case law cited: Function Media v. Google; ePlus v. Lawson; In re Aoyama; Typhoon Touch; Aristocrat; WMS Gaming (examples of requiring disclosure of corresponding structure or algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: If applicant does not intend to invoke §112(f), require identification or addition of structure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not intend to invoke section 112(f), and the structural component of the claim element is not obvious, the applicant should be required to identify the structure in the claim element that performs the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant cannot satisfactorily point to structure in the claim itself that performs the claimed function, the examiner should (or should) require the applicant to amend the claim to add such structure. This prevents purely functional claim language from escaping §112(f) limits by avoiding the phrase 'means for.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject or treat as means-plus-function when appropriate and make scope-limiting basis explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant does not provide appropriate structure for a claim element, the examiner can reject the claim for failure to comply with section 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the examiner can point out the absence of structure and proceed to examine the claim as a means-plus-function claim. If an examiner takes the latter course, he should make explicit on the record that the claim is being allowed only because the broadest reasonable interpretation of that claim is nonetheless limited to the structure disclosed in the specification and equivalents thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify on the record what applicant regards as equivalents to disclosed structure
rubrics_metrics.description: In some circumstances it may be appropriate to clarify on the record what the applicant regards as equivalent to that structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an applicant seeks to distinguish prior art on the ground that the structure she discloses is different than that in the prior art, it would be helpful to establish on the record whether the applicant regards those two structures as equivalent. Doing so helps resolve later disputes about claim scope and equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use on-the-record determinations to identify and limit functional claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: By establishing on the record whether a claim element invokes section 112(f) and what structure it covers, examiners can help identify functional claims and limit them to their proper scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive on-the-record clarification (invocation, corresponding structure, and equivalence) enables examiners to reject applications that improperly seek to control all ways of performing a function and reduces overbroad functional claiming that fuels invalid claims and troll litigation.
